evidence.note: CONFIRMED claim: the gitleaks Secrets check (scripts/ci/gitleaks-pushed.sh over origin/main..HEAD) flags ddflow's synthetic gitlab PAT filler sample (gitlab-pat rule) quoted in the committed event-log shard .ddflow/events/lane-hard.jsonl (from a critic finding on AU-redact-shapes). Probe: gitleaks git --config .gitleaks.toml --log-opts=origin/main..HEAD reported 'leaks found: 2' (both RuleID=gitlab-pat, Secret= [REDACTED] on the unfixed config; after adding the exact-value allowlist entry the same scan reports 'no leaks found'. A real glpat- token in an event shard still fires (regression test asserts exit!=0).

chunk_findings.detail: The new allowlist regex itself spells the full GitLab-PAT-shaped value `glpat-Xk3Zq9LmFk3Zq9LmFk3Z` inside `.gitleaks.toml`, but the allowlist is scoped with `condition = "AND"` to paths matching only `.ddflow/events/[^/]+.jsonl`. When the CI runs gitleaks over the pushed commit containing this change, the GitLab PAT rule will match the literal in `.gitleaks.toml`; the finding’s path is `.gitleaks.toml`, not an event shard, so the new allowlist does not suppress it. The fix therefore can still fail the same “gitleaks over the pushed commits” check on its own config file, while the regression tests do not catch this because they only scan a temporary `.ddflow/events/a.jsonl` file.

chunk_findings.detail: The new allowlist regex line embeds a complete GitLab-PAT-shaped value, `glpat-Xk3Zq9LmFk3Zq9LmFk3Z`, in the tracked config file itself. When the CI check scans the pushed merge commit, it will scan `.gitleaks.toml` as a changed file, and the `gitlab-pat` rule can match that literal. The new allowlist cannot suppress it because its `paths` pattern is only `^\.ddflow/events/[^/]+\.jsonl$`, not `.gitleaks.toml`. Thus, given the commit containing this config change, gitleaks still fails on the config file even though the event-shard value is allowlisted. The tests do not catch this because they only scan `.ddflow/events/a.jsonl`, not the modified `.gitleaks.toml`.
chunk_findings.title: .gitleaks.toml:154

chunk_findings.detail: The new allowlist only matches paths `^\.ddflow/events/[^/]+\.jsonl$`, but the literal secret `glpat-Xk3Zq9LmFk3Zq9LmFk3Z` is written unescaped into `.gitleaks.toml` itself (TOML `'''...'''` keeps that substring intact). The default `gitlab-pat` rule matches `glpat-` plus 20 word characters, so a repo scan of `.gitleaks.toml` still reports that line; the new tests only call `_scan_committed` on `.ddflow/events/a.jsonl` and never see it. The prior JWT allowlist avoided this by storing `\.` in the file so the raw text is not a live secret. Given a scan of this commit, gitleaks still fails, just on the config instead of the event shard.
